divergences: Reference/golden model: Impl 1 self-checks via z3 proofs + a single e2e_N=16 whole-system equivalence; Impl 2 adds an independent schoolbook negacyclic-convolution AND direct O(N^2) DFT golden — the spec never pins which reference behavior the impl must equal, so each invented its own correctness oracle.

Output ordering: both embed a bit-reversed psi/twiddle table and relabel to natural order, but neither could reproduce the paper's 'no bit-reversal' natural-order datapath — the spec leaves the rearranged-loop addressing open, so both fell back to the same reconstruction (a shared guess, not a spec-pinned fact).

Radix-4 fused butterfly: both verify only the DFT4 identity (2-mult count asserted), neither reproduces the actual symmetric-operator 2-mult sharing mechanism — the spec gives only the 2/3 and 8/10 counts, not the formula.
Barrett conditional-subtract count: spec is internally inconsistent ('exactly 2' vs '<=2' vs 'one conditional subtract'); both impls independently chose '<=2 for x in [0,(q-1)^2]' to resolve it.
FSM transition table: spec carries three contradictory state lists; each impl reconstructed its own (Impl 2: IDLE->LOAD->RUN_STAGE/NEXT_STAGE->SCALE->DRAIN->DONE), source-missing.
Naive radix-4 add/sub baseline (10) used to anchor the 20% claim is reconstructed by both, not given.

structural_findings: The defining contribution — the conflict-free bank/offset map and per-stage crossbar — is replaced by a reconstructed XOR-fold; the architecture is functionally equivalent but is NOT the paper's specific mapping.
Both retain a bit-reversed intermediate then relabel, directly contradicting the paper's natural-order / no-bit-reversal datapath.

The fused two-stage radix-4 schedule that realizes the 2-mult/8-add-sub savings is collapsed to a recursive/textbook radix-4 DIT verified only by the DFT4 identity, not the paper's symmetric-operator datapath.
Host PCIe/DMA/AXI-Stream boundary and the cycle-accurate 9-stage pipeline are omitted entirely — modeled as pure functional transforms.

summary: Reproducibility is moderate: the spec pins the full functional parameter set (N, q=12289, psi/omega/Ninv, Barrett mu/k, 8 BU, 14-bit widths) so the two impls agree almost everywhere, but the paper's headline structures — the conflict-free Sec.III bank/offset map, the natural-order no-bit-reversal addressing, the fused 2-mult radix-4 schedule, and a consistent FSM and Barrett-correction bound — are source-missing, forcing shared reconstructions. Fidelity is mid: every recoverable parameter matches and the negacyclic round-trip identity holds, but the system's actual differentiators (no bit-reversal, the specific conflict-free mapping, the symmetric-operator savings) are violated or unverifiable, so the impls are closer to a generic correct negacyclic NTT than to the precise CFNTT architecture.

guessed: Forward/inverse butterfly convention -> CT/DIT forward, GS/DIF inverse (Longa-Naehrig merged psi-twist negacyclic); spec only pins 'DIT, merged psi-twist'
Fast-NTT output ordering -> standard bit-reversed output reindexed to natural (the committed ROM embeds bit-reversal, contradicting the paper's no-bit-reversal claim which I could not reproduce)
Twiddle-ROM address function f(stage,block) -> standard (1<<stage)+block with bit-reversed psi-power table; paper's rearranged-loop addressing is source-missing
Per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s -> taken as the permutation induced by the committed bank() (sigma_s = bank^-1 at stride 2^s); paper's table not transcribed
Conflict-free bank()/offset() -> committed XOR-fold bank(i)=(i&7)^((i>>3)&7)^((i>>6)&7)^((i>>9)&1), offset(i)=i>>3; paper's Sec.III functions not transcribed
Radix-4 fused 2-mult symmetric schedule -> verified only as the DFT4 identity y_t=sum in[m]*j^{tm} with j=psi^512; the actual 2-vs-3-mult sharing mechanism is source-missing
Barrett conditional-subtract count -> <=2 subtractions for x in [0,(q-1)^2] (spec is internally inconsistent: 'exactly 2' vs '<=2', 'one conditional subtract' elsewhere)
e2e small size root psi16 -> psi^(2048/32)=1945^64 mod 12289 (order 32, 16th power = -1), per spec verification.e2e_N=16
Host/PCIe/DMA AXI-Stream framing -> not modeled functionally (spec marks the whole host boundary reproduction-invented / source-missing)
modulus q -> 12289 (ref-impl value; paper body only says '14-bit NTT-friendly prime')

Exact merged-negacyclic NTT algorithm -> standard Longa-Naehrig CT/DIT forward (bit-reversed psi table) + GS/DIF inverse with final N^-1 scale; spec pins only 'DIT merged psi-twist' / 'GS inverse' and a bit-reversed ROM layout
Reference golden for correctness -> schoolbook negacyclic convolution in Z_q[x]/(x^N+1) and a direct O(N^2) DFT; spec gives only properties, not a reference model

Radix-4 butterfly equations -> taken verbatim from the exploded-view part (y0..y3 with j=omega^(N/4) constant rotator); verified to equal a recursive radix-4 DIT == direct DFT, but the paper's *fused two-stage conflict-free schedule* is source-missing
Conflict-free bank/offset map -> bank(i)=(i&7)^((i>>3)&7)^((i>>6)&7)^((i>>9)&1), offset(i)=i>>3 (the spec's committed XOR-fold; paper's Sec.III function is undecodable)
Per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s -> defined as bank()-induced routing; paper's explicit table is source-missing

Twiddle-ROM address f(stage,block) -> (1<<stage)+block with bit-reversed contents; this still embeds bit-reversal, contradicting the headline 'no bit-reversal' claim which the source does not let me reconstruct
FSM transition table -> reconstructed IDLE->LOAD->RUN_STAGE/NEXT_STAGE->(SCALE if INTT)->DRAIN->DONE->IDLE; paper's exact table is source-missing
Barrett conditional-subtract count -> <=2 subtractions, proven sufficient for x in [0,(q-1)^2]
Host PCIe/DMA/AXI-Stream boundary -> omitted from the functional model entirely (spec itself flags it as reproduction-invented, not in the paper)

8-way simultaneous bank distinctness -> only pairwise (per butterfly operand pair) distinctness proven for every stride; full 8-lane no-conflict at one cycle is asserted by the map but not exhaustively proven here
